content.text:
1. Sunlight contains many colors, which together appear white.
2. As sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it encounters tiny air molecules.
3. Those molecules scatter shorter wavelengths of light more strongly than longer ones. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red, so it gets scattered in many directions.
4. That scattered blue light reaches your eyes from across the sky, making the sky look blue.

Violet light scatters even more, but the Sun emits less of it, and our eyes are less sensitive to violet—so blue dominates what we see.
